cards.title: Signup Form A/B Test Priority Order
cards.summary: Test signup form variables in descending order of leverage, starting with the offer.
cards.use_when: Planning the next round of opt-in experiments, or deciding which variable to change when form volume is too low to test everything at once.

cards.title: Configure a Signup A/B Test: Manual 50/50 and Winner Selection
cards.summary: Set the traffic split manually rather than automatic so the platform does not call a winner on insufficient volume.
cards.use_when: Launching an A/B test on a popup or form inside your email platform.

cards.title: Full-Screen Opt-In Forms and Zero-Party Data Quizzes
cards.summary: Use full-screen branded popups with a single question to capture intent data alongside the email address.
cards.use_when: Choosing a capture format, or adding a segmentation question at the point of opt-in for a Shopify store.

cards.title: Gamified Opt-In First Steps: Spin-to-Win and Scratch-Off
cards.summary: Test interactive first steps before the email field, using a guaranteed-win mechanic, and expect different winners per audience.
cards.use_when: Choosing the opening interaction on a full-screen capture form to raise engagement and signup rate.

cards.title: Deliverability Hygiene: Authentication, Engagement Tiers and List Cleaning
cards.summary: Implement SPF, DKIM and DMARC, segment by engagement recency, and suppress long-inactive subscribers to protect inbox placement.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing sending infrastructure and list health, especially before scaling campaign volume.

cards.title: Core Automated Flows to Build and the 72-Hour Purchase Window
cards.summary: Prioritise five automated flows, and treat the first 72 hours of a new subscriber's life as the highest-converting window.
cards.use_when: Deciding which lifecycle automations to build or fix next in an ecommerce email program.

cards.title: Email Campaign Cadence and Audience Strategy
cards.summary: Plan campaign volume around a 3–4 per week cadence, sent with a real strategy rather than ad hoc.
cards.use_when: Setting or reviewing the weekly campaign calendar and checking whether sends are strategic or random.

cards.title: Use AI and Personalisation Tools Only After the Fundamentals Are In Place
cards.summary: Layer personalisation, zero-party data quizzes and split-tested desktop/mobile experiences onto a working capture-flow-campaign foundation rather than as a substitute for it.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in AI personalisation, quiz tools or advanced targeting features before fixing list growth, flows or deliverability.

cards.title: Choose a popup first step: scratch-off, quiz, or micro-commitment
cards.summary: Evaluate three popup first-step formats (scratch-off, mini quiz, micro-commitment) to raise email signup rate before the email field appears.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to structure the first screen of your email capture popup so more store visitors begin the signup interaction.

cards.title: Decide whether the popup success page reveals the discount code or sends to email
cards.summary: Trade off immediate code delivery against first-email engagement and deliverability when configuring the signup success page.
cards.use_when: Configuring the success/reward step of your email signup popup and choosing between showing the discount immediately or routing the subscriber to their inbox.

cards.title: Configure single vs double opt-in for popup signup forms
cards.summary: Choose email signup confirmation separately from how and when the promised reward is delivered.
cards.use_when: Setting the opt-in method on your signup form, which determines whether the discount is shown on-screen or delivered by email.

cards.title: Set popup trigger timing, scroll depth, and exit intent
cards.summary: Configure time-delay, scroll-depth and exit-intent triggers for signup popups, with a 4s vs 12s test as the starting point.
cards.use_when: Choosing when the email capture popup appears on your store, to avoid interrupting visitors too early or missing them entirely.

cards.title: Build signup-form targeting rules for new vs returning visitors
cards.summary: Use targeting rules to show a first-time capture popup to new visitors and separate popups to already-subscribed visitors.
cards.use_when: Setting up popup audiences so you capture new emails without annoying existing subscribers, or to collect extra data from people already on your list.

cards.title: Preview and QA signup popups across devices before publishing
cards.summary: Use preview and device-simulation tools to confirm the popup renders and animates correctly everywhere before pushing it live.
cards.use_when: Final QA before publishing a new email capture popup to your live storefront.

cards.title: Offer copy for signups: explicit discount vs mystery discount
cards.summary: Test mystery or exclusive offer copy against explicit percentage-off copy, especially at lower discount levels.
cards.use_when: Writing the headline and button copy of a signup popup to raise signup rate without changing your actual discount.

cards.title: Diagnose a monetization problem before blaming email or buying more traffic
cards.summary: Frame list and welcome-flow weakness as a monetization problem that leaks paid traffic and inflates CAC.
cards.use_when: Reviewing why paid acquisition costs keep rising and deciding whether to invest in welcome flows rather than more ad spend.

cards.title: Front-load the welcome flow around the first 72 hours
cards.summary: Structure the welcome flow to concentrate persuasion and sends in the first 72 hours after signup when momentum and intent peak.
cards.use_when: Designing or restructuring the welcome series cadence for new email subscribers.

cards.title: Set welcome flow trigger filters and disable smart sending
cards.summary: Configure the welcome flow entry trigger, zero-purchase filter, no re-entry, and per-email send settings so only new non-buyers get the welcome discount.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing the welcome flow automation settings in your ESP.

cards.title: Write welcome email 1A: deliver the code above the fold
cards.summary: Make the first welcome email a frictionless delivery of the promised code with product guidance and trust builders directly in the above-the-fold area.
cards.use_when: Drafting or rewriting the first email of the welcome series.

cards.title: Send a same-day plain-text founder reminder as welcome email 1B
cards.summary: Add a short, human plain-text second email eight hours after the first to capture day-zero momentum.
cards.use_when: Adding a second welcome-flow email on the day of signup to recover subscribers who didn't buy immediately.

cards.title: Use welcome email 2 to build brand trust with substance, not fluff
cards.summary: Answer 'who are you and why should I trust you' in a short trust-building email with a discount reminder and CTA.
cards.use_when: Writing the second-day welcome email that establishes credibility for new subscribers who haven't bought yet.

cards.title: Use welcome email 3 to guide overwhelmed subscribers to a first purchase
cards.summary: Reduce choice paralysis by naming one to three bestsellers with benefit-led positioning and a discount reminder.
cards.use_when: Writing the welcome-flow email that helps undecided subscribers pick a first product.

cards.title: Welcome email 4: handle objections and differentiate at the product or category level
cards.summary: Answer unasked objections about price, quality and alternatives, then add real urgency tied to a credible discount code.
cards.use_when: Writing the welcome-flow email that targets subscribers still hesitating after the first three sends.

cards.title: Welcome email 5: escalate urgency with reviews that mirror buyer objections
cards.summary: Push for the first purchase using a tightened deadline and one to three specific, pain-point-matching reviews.
cards.use_when: Writing the welcome-flow email that uses a closing deadline plus social proof to convert hesitant subscribers.

cards.title: Welcome email 6: close with a final reason to act, and test the format
cards.summary: Deliver the final welcome-flow push with the offer, strong urgency, and either a designed or plain-text format chosen by testing.
cards.use_when: Writing the final email of the welcome series and choosing its format.

cards.title: Add proven evergreen campaigns to the welcome flow for extra revenue
cards.summary: Extend the welcome series beyond the core emails by appending evergreen campaigns that performed well as broadcasts.
cards.use_when: Looking for incremental welcome-flow revenue after the core six-email structure is working.

cards.title: Position browse abandonment as mid-funnel persuasion, not lost-sale recovery
cards.summary: Treat browse-abandonment emails as trust and objection-handling plays for comparing shoppers rather than as discount-driven cart recovery.
cards.use_when: Deciding the strategy and tone for a browse abandonment flow targeting product-page visitors who didn't add to cart.

cards.title: Set browse abandonment trigger filters and a 30-day cooldown
cards.summary: Configure the viewed-product trigger with zero-order, zero-checkout, zero-add-to-cart filters and a 30-day re-entry limit.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing the browse abandonment flow in your ESP so it fires only for genuinely unconverted browsers.

cards.title: Time the browse abandonment delays and use dynamic product blocks
cards.summary: Set the send delay by intent level and include a dynamic product block plus recommendations in every browse-abandonment email.
cards.use_when: Building the timing and core content of the browse abandonment sequence.

cards.title: Write browse abandonment email 1 as a light, timely reminder
cards.summary: Send a non-aggressive product reminder within hours of the page view, with a dynamic product block, recommendations and social proof.
cards.use_when: Drafting the first browse-abandonment email.

cards.title: Write browse abandonment email 2 to remove friction, not add pressure
cards.summary: Lead with risk reversals, social proof and product guidance to address hesitation for comparison shoppers.
cards.use_when: Writing the second browse-abandonment email for viewers who ignored the first reminder.

cards.title: Browse abandonment email 3: diagnose hesitation type before escalating with a discount
cards.summary: Classify remaining hesitation as price sensitivity, comparison shopping, or procrastination and escalate the offer intelligently.
cards.use_when: Writing the third browse-abandonment email, where the audience has ignored both the reminder and the trust-building email.

cards.title: Browse abandonment flow: 3-4 email escalation ladder
cards.summary: Structure a browse abandonment flow that escalates from reminder to trust-building to deadline-driven discount or subscription push over 4 emails.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing the browse abandonment flow for your store.

cards.title: Abandoned cart vs abandoned checkout: build side by side
cards.summary: Use the same flow structure for abandoned cart and abandoned checkout, differing only in trigger and one flow filter.
cards.use_when: Setting up abandoned cart and abandoned checkout flows inside Klaviyo (verify current interface).

cards.title: Abandoned cart/checkout email content: 3-stage objection sequence
cards.summary: Content plan for what each abandoned cart/checkout email should contain: simple reminder, plastic-text founder check-in, then objection handling.
cards.use_when: Writing the copy for abandoned cart and abandoned checkout emails before any discount is offered.

cards.title: Discount vs no-discount fork: non-buyers vs returning customers
cards.summary: Split abandoned cart/checkout discounting: offer an escalating discount to first-time non-buyers, but only support or a smaller incentive to returning customers.
cards.use_when: Deciding who gets a discount code in your abandoned cart/checkout flow and how much.

cards.title: Post-purchase flow filters and timing
cards.summary: Set up a post-purchase flow with the right filters, filters that skip recent emailers, and a 10-minute first email delay.
cards.use_when: Setting up a post-purchase flow in Klaviyo that turns first-time buyers into repeat customers.

cards.title: Post-purchase email content: 6-email sequence
cards.summary: Content plan for the post-purchase emails that reduce returns, build the relationship, and drive the first repeat purchase.
cards.use_when: Writing the emails in your post-purchase flow after a customer's first order.

cards.title: Post-purchase as the retention engine
cards.summary: Treat the first purchase as the start of the relationship, not the finish line, and use the post-purchase flow to drive repeat purchase and reduce returns.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much post-purchase and replenishment effort to invest after the first order.

cards.title: Email campaign frequency: aim for 3-4 per week
cards.summary: Send email campaigns 3-4 times per week so your brand stays top of mind without burning out the list.
cards.use_when: Deciding how often to send email campaigns to your ecommerce list.

cards.title: Campaign mix: don't let promos dominate the calendar
cards.summary: Balance your campaign calendar across seven categories instead of leaning on discounts, or you train subscribers to wait for sales.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing your monthly/quarterly email campaign calendar.

cards.title: Non-discounted campaign idea bank (social proof + education)
cards.summary: A list of social proof and educational campaign angles you can send without discounting.
cards.use_when: Filling your campaign calendar with non-discounted emails that build trust with your list.

cards.title: Non-discounted campaign idea bank (product, brand, occasion, engagement)
cards.summary: Product-focused, brand/culture, occasion and interactive campaign angles that sell without discounts.
cards.use_when: Planning campaign emails that highlight products or brand story rather than cutting price.

cards.title: Campaign calendar tool setup and the minimum fields to track
cards.summary: Maintain a campaign calendar in any tool, tracking status, ownership, content and results at minimum.
cards.use_when: Setting up or cleaning up the production calendar your team uses to plan campaign emails.

cards.title: Run a campaign calendar in a tool your team will actually open
cards.summary: Choose the lightest project tool your team already uses, then track six fields per campaign.
cards.use_when: Setting up or replacing the email campaign planning system before a month of sends.

cards.title: Send campaigns only to engaged subscribers
cards.summary: Suppress unengaged profiles from campaigns to protect deliverability and inbox placement.
cards.use_when: Deciding the send list for any ecommerce campaign, especially after engagement or revenue has declined.

cards.title: Anchor the calendar with fixed dates before filling content
cards.summary: Lock non-negotiable sends first, then build all remaining campaigns around them.
cards.use_when: Starting a new month of email campaign planning for a store with launches, restocks, or planned promotions.

cards.title: Keep sales events to one per month or fewer
cards.summary: Rare promotions preserve full-price conversion and avoid training customers to wait for discounts.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many discount or sale emails to schedule in a month and how to protect margin.

cards.title: Reuse existing blog, video and social content for campaigns
cards.summary: Mine your own content library before writing anything new, and match each piece to the right season.
cards.use_when: Filling empty calendar slots for a store that lacks new creative bandwidth.

cards.title: Plan a month of campaigns with an AI context block
cards.summary: Feed AI brand, audience, cadence, fixed dates and a campaign-idea list, then refine its draft.
cards.use_when: Drafting a full month of email campaign ideas quickly instead of brainstorming from a blank calendar.

cards.title: Pressure-test the finished calendar with AI before finalizing
cards.summary: Paste the completed calendar into AI to flag imbalance, repetition and over-promotion before it goes live.
cards.use_when: Doing a final quality check on a completed monthly email calendar.

cards.title: Check monthly mix across the seven campaign categories
cards.summary: Audit campaign balance by category before finalizing, pulling anything above roughly one-third promotional.
cards.use_when: Finalizing a monthly email campaign calendar and checking whether it is too sales-heavy.

cards.title: Alternate campaign types within each week, not just across the month
cards.summary: Avoid clustering similar campaign types in one week — no two consecutive emails should share a type.
cards.use_when: Sequencing a week of sends and checking why engagement dips despite a balanced monthly mix.

cards.title: Build a two-week execution buffer before sends go out
cards.summary: Always have emails two weeks ahead — written, designed and sitting ready for review.
cards.use_when: Fixing late, rushed campaign production that degrades email quality and coverage.

cards.title: Run a 20–30 minute monthly performance review
cards.summary: Review opens, clicks and revenue by campaign each month to find patterns the calendar can encode.
cards.use_when: End-of-month review before planning the next month's email calendar.

cards.title: Put the product in every email, leading with value
cards.summary: Even non-promotional emails should present the product as the natural solution to a taught problem.
cards.use_when: Writing education, brand or social proof campaigns that risk becoming product-free content.

cards.title: Restrict SMS campaigns to launches, restocks and sales
cards.summary: Use SMS sparingly for highest-impact moments and keep routine sends in email.
cards.use_when: Deciding which campaign calendar items get SMS versus email, especially outside the US.

cards.title: Build a systematic AB testing mindset before running tests
cards.summary: Test on a schedule, from written hypotheses, with enough data, judged on revenue.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ecommerce email testing program or auditing why past tests produced no usable learning.

cards.title: Rank signup form tests by impact and work top-down
cards.summary: Start with the offer, then micro-step, delay, form type, copy, design, and finally SMS angle.
cards.use_when: Prioritizing which signup form (popup) experiments to run first to grow the email list.

cards.title: Choose signup form images by device, not aesthetics
cards.summary: Use human faces or pets on desktop forms, skip images on mobile to protect load speed.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether and which image to place in a popup or signup form.

cards.title: Test SMS signup angles against the email offer
cards.summary: Compare same-offer, better-offer and VIP-club angles for adding SMS subscribers.
cards.use_when: Building or optimizing the SMS opt-in step, especially when email signup already exists.

cards.title: Test the first email of every flow first
cards.summary: The first flow email carries by far the highest impact — spend limited testing time there.
cards.use_when: Allocating limited experimentation capacity across abandoned cart, browse, checkout, welcome and winback flows.

cards.title: Test flow time delays with flow-type reference ranges
cards.summary: Tune when the first flow email fires, using source ranges by abandonment type.
cards.use_when: Setting or testing send delays in site, browse, cart and checkout abandonment flows.

cards.title: Test product blocks, dynamic feeds and hero images in flows
cards.summary: Compare recommendation formats and email structure to raise flow revenue.
cards.use_when: Optimizing abandoned browse, cart and checkout emails, and cross-sell or winback flows.

cards.title: Test plain-text vs designed emails and copy variables in flows
cards.summary: Plain-text founder messages, copy length, tone and angle are high-impact flow tests worth running.
cards.use_when: Deciding email format and copy style for flow emails, particularly discount-bearing final emails.

cards.title: Test landing page destinations from flow emails
cards.summary: Compare collection page, product page, homepage and dedicated landing pages on end revenue.
cards.use_when: Choosing where flow or campaign email links should send shoppers.

cards.title: Use manual 50/50 splits instead of automatic winner selection
cards.summary: Avoid staggered sends that deliver the winning variant at a suboptimal time on early, noisy data.
cards.use_when: Configuring any Klaviyo AB test for campaigns or flows.

cards.title: Run systematic campaign-side tests, starting with send time
cards.summary: Send time is a top campaign variable; also test angles, landing pages, feeds, subject lines and sender names.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to test on recurring newsletter-style campaigns rather than flows.

cards.title: Deprioritize subject line, sender name and CTA button tests
cards.summary: These are easy but low-impact — run them after the high-impact tests are exhausted.
cards.use_when: Choosing which email tests to run when testing capacity is limited.

cards.title: Set the upper bound on test duration and sample per variant
cards.summary: Aim for around two weeks per test and at least 1,000 recipients per variant before concluding.
cards.use_when: Deciding when to call an email AB test and move to the next one.

cards.title: Build segments that start with marketing eligibility
cards.summary: Every Klaviyo segment should first filter on who can legally receive marketing, with extra GDPR handling in Europe.
cards.use_when: Creating or auditing send segments for campaigns and flows, especially in Europe.

cards.title: Build an engaged-90-day segment as your campaign workhorse
cards.summary: Construct an engaged segment combining email and site activity with OR logic, then clone it across 14/30/60/90/120-day windows.
cards.use_when: Setting up campaign send audiences or starting deliverability recovery in Klaviyo.

cards.title: Mandatory exclusion segments for every campaign
cards.summary: Create suppression segments for spam markers and bounced addresses and apply them to all sends.
cards.use_when: Before sending any campaign, or during a list-cleaning pass.

cards.title: Build unengaged segments that exclude past customers
cards.summary: Create 120-day and 180-day unengaged segments using AND logic that quarantine never-purchasers but retain past buyers.
cards.use_when: Building sunset flows and long-term suppression rules to protect deliverability and reduce Klaviyo costs.

cards.title: Specialty segments for buyer-stage targeting
cards.summary: Create first-time buyer, returning customer, non-buyer and VIP segments to target differentiated offers.
cards.use_when: Planning sales events, loyalty messaging or new-customer reactivation offers.

cards.title: Diagnose deliverability with placement testing and Klaviyo metrics
cards.summary: Use inbox placement tools and Klaviyo's deliverability tab to find whether the problem is placement, provider or geography.
cards.use_when: Open rates are consistently low and you need to locate the cause before changing strategy.

cards.title: Four-step technical setup for email sending
cards.summary: Configure branded sending domain, default sender, DMARC and optionally BIMI as the baseline deliverability setup.
cards.use_when: Initial Klaviyo setup or auditing an account with unexplained placement problems.

cards.title: Five-step list-cleaning protocol
cards.summary: Suppress five categories of dead weight to cut costs and improve sender reputation.
cards.use_when: Any account with a large list and low engagement, or as a periodic hygiene pass.

cards.title: Ramp deliverability back with a staged engagement ladder
cards.summary: Recover inbox placement by sending only to progressively wider engaged segments while watching open rate gates.
cards.use_when: A store has a known deliverability problem (consistently low opens, spam complaints) and needs a recovery sequence.

cards.title: Make emails readable to Gmail's AI filter
cards.summary: Replace image-only email elements with live text so AI inbox systems can parse and prioritize your emails.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing campaign templates for inbox placement.
